P1.evidence: No setter code on this call, but an application exists and the rep had plainly not read it — the prospect referenced it himself while answering a question the form had already covered: 'I think I even put it in the little question or everything'. Nothing was read back. The frame was the rep's standard two-part version with a courtesy addition: 'I just want to get a good idea where you're at. Really build out what it is that you want to achieve. And then if there's alignment, we can talk about the coaching. If not, that's fine as well. I'll point you in the right direction anyway.' Still no 'what's in the way' or 'what you need'. Agreement requested and given ('All right?' / 'Sure. Sure.'), and the open question ran verbatim.

P2.evidence: Much the strongest baseline in the batch. The health question was asked properly and directly, which is what surfaced the diagnosis: 'what was going on with the joints? Just so I'm clear, was there any like diagnosis or anything like that? Or is it all good?' Training was covered ('Are you doing anything with kettlebells now? Not doing anything at the gyms or anything like that?'), results were probed hard via the 10-point scale and the excellent follow-up 'Okay, what makes you say a 4?', and sleep and energy were asked explicitly — the only call in the batch where they were: 'I guess the last thing I would check is sleep and energy. How's that kind of throughout the day?' The two failures matter though. Age, height and current weight were never asked of a man whose primary tangible goal is weight loss and who peaked at 280 lb. Occupation was never asked either; it emerged only incidentally when the rep noticed a badge and asked 'Are you in the military?'. Injury duration was never established.

P3.evidence: The best goals work in the batch. Tangible outcome was pushed for properly: 'if we were to fast-forward six months... What outcome you're going for? Try and be as tangible and as specific as you can.' The can't-do-it-now question ran and produced the strongest material on the call: 'What kind of stuff comes top of mind?' — 'Like just getting down on the ground, crawling around with kids, jumping.' The drive-through to fatherhood genuinely happened, though the rep asserted it rather than asking: 'That's a strong why. I always find that the people who have young kids or got a kid on the way, they get the best results because the biggest reason is looking you in your face every day', and later 'your kid would come out and see just this jacked, feeling good David. What a way to start its life.' What is missing is the bridge and the deepening. He never asked what is actually driving this outside the physical, never asked what moving better would do for him, and never asked who else it impacts — the kids arrived because the prospect volunteered them. The reflect-back was early and thematic rather than the scripted reframe: 'Sounds like you're out of the boiling water. Now you're on the way up and you just kind of want to lift on the way up.'

P4.evidence: One check ran, and it ran well — the rep let the prospect name his own gap with a genuinely good framing: 'Some people, it's accountability. Some people, it's I need someone to wake me up at 5am and tell me what to do. Some people, it's like I'll do it, just tell me what to do... What do you feel like is important for you at this point?' That produced 'First would be just accountability. Not necessarily hey, get up, go do it. But like, hey, did you go do it?' plus the request for form critique. Everything else was skipped. The prospect had handed over a rich failure history unprompted — multiple unused gym memberships, running until his knees stopped him, gluten-free, keto — and none of it was asked about or examined. No 'why do you feel it didn't stick', no 'the information isn't the problem'.

P5.evidence: No consequence frame. Not one of the four checks was attempted. This is the most costly omission on the call given what was available: a man who could not stand at a sink for five minutes, who has a spinal diagnosis and knee flare-ups, and who has a third child arriving. 'If nothing changes, what does life look like over the next two years' writes itself here and was never asked, so when the price arrived there was no accumulated cost of inaction to weigh it against — only a household mid-austerity.

P6.evidence: A process check stood in for the belief question and got a warm answer: 'In terms of the process, how do you feel about it?' — 'Well, I like the sound of it... That sounds like the best of all the worlds.' The all-in question was never asked, and on this call that omission is decisive: 'if you had everything you needed, is there any reason you wouldn't go all in on this?' would have surfaced Rachel and the household spending rule before a number existed, instead of after. The rep did eventually isolate personal commitment, but only reactively, inside the spouse objection at 00:28:07.

P11.evidence: A close was attempted so the phase applies. No payment collected. The onboarding call was proposed for Monday or Tuesday and the rep correctly stated the sequencing — 'to be able to book that in, obviously we've got to, like, payment done, all that sort of stuff first' — but nothing was booked. No agreement email, no signature on the call, no welcome email, Skool link or onboarding questionnaire instruction. Closed on an open-ended 'I'll text you and you just let me know'.

objection_plays.detail: Trigger at 00:24:45: 'I would definitely have to discuss it with my wife before I say yes to that.' The best objection handling in the batch, and still incomplete. Ran: permission and rapport ('I'm not going to say you can't do that, David'), her support for the journey ('Is she supportive of you in this journey you're on?'), what obstacles might come up — delivered as the two-reactions framing, which is effective and got an honest read ('I feel probably the first one'), the if-she-says-no question, and the personal-yes isolation ('if she said yeah, would you do it? Like, is it something that you want to do?' — 'It is something I want to do'). Not run: 'money aside, do you personally feel this CAN get you to your goal' asked before the price rather than after, 'is there any reason she would NOT want you stronger and less in pain', the permission-versus-input challenge, the 'this isn't a joint decision like buying a house' ownership move, and the deposit-with-full-refund fallback, which was the obvious play once the prospect said he expected a no.

Money trigger at 00:24:45 ('that is significant enough') and again at 00:28:12 ('the pure cost of it is a little, ooh!'). One move ran — the reframe, 'I think of it as 6,000 reasons why you will stick to it' — plus the guarantee as risk reduction. Everything else missed, and the miss is unusually costly because the prospect opened the door himself at 00:26:36 with an unprompted description of his household finances: raises every year, no surplus, active spending cutbacks. That is an invitation to the financial picture. Not one of the six questions followed — no cash on hand, no monthly leftover, no credit cards, no available credit, no investments — and no payment plan was mentioned, on the one call in this batch where instalments were the obvious solution.

Script gap — clinical fit, and the most serious instance in the batch. The prospect disclosed a named diagnosis of ankylosing spondylitis, a chronic inflammatory spinal condition, plus continuing knee flare-ups and a history of back failure under trivial static load. The playbook has no clearance gate, so the rep closed the topic with 'The doctors are interesting. They tell you everything' and moved to the next question. What the script needs here is not a rebuttal but a mandatory stop: confirm the diagnosis, ask whether a clinician has cleared loaded ballistic training, and defer the guarantee until they have.

notes: Process-wise this is the rep's strongest call in the batch — real baseline including sleep and energy, real goals depth, a genuine spouse play — and it still stalled because the all-in question was never asked before the number, so the wife and the household spending freeze both surfaced after the price rather than before it. Two corrections: ask the all-in question pre-price, and when a prospect volunteers 'the money's just going out the door', run the financial picture and put a payment plan on the table. Separately and more urgently: a named ankylosing spondylitis diagnosis must trigger a clearance question, not a joke about doctors.
